Instagram has really gone downhill over the years, and it's hard to ignore the company's unethical practices and obsession with profit over user experience. First, the app is notorious for its data-stealing tendencies. Instagram collects vast amounts of personal information, often without clear consent or transparency. It feels like the platform is constantly tracking you, from what you like to where you go, all in an effort to sell your data to advertisers. The idea that your every move is monetized is unsettling, and there's very little control or accountability on Instagram's part.

Functionality-wise, Instagram has become a mess. The interface is cluttered, outdated, and user-unfriendly. What used to be a straightforward app is now buried under layers of ads, stories, and recommendations you didn’t ask for. The algorithm seems more focused on pushing sponsored content and irrelevant posts than showing you what you actually want to see. Every update brings more confusion and frustration, with features being broken or hidden behind confusing menus.

At this point, Instagram feels less like a fun social platform and more like a corporate machine designed to harvest data and maximize profits. The app's original charm has been overshadowed by constant ads, privacy concerns, and a lack of innovation. It's hard to recommend Instagram to anyone who values their privacy or a good user experience. There are much better alternatives out there.

I like Instagram. I do. It’s a good app for keeping in contact with friends and for being able to share the things I create as an artist. But I swear the app gets worse with every update. The changes to the layout of the home page that make it so it’s basically a second explore page and so you don’t see posts from those you follow in chronological order are frustrating. The change to messages that make it so swiping prompts a reply to someone rather than exiting is confusing and non-intuitive, not to mention outright useless. The changes to the placement of the notification and posting tabs are infuriating. This is an app for sharing, not for shopping. Keep the shopping tab out of the main tab bar and put reels back with explore.

Instagram would be much more user friendly if there was an option to toggle certain features (although calling them features instead of “hinderances” might, in some cases, be generous), such as the swipe-to-reply in messages, the suggested posts after the most recent posts in the home section, or whether posts were ordered algorithmically or chronologically. Additionally, allowing users to set up the layout of their tab bar would also make it more user friendly. I’m sure someone out there prefers the easy access to the reels tab, and would want to keep it where it currently is. But most don’t. Thus, allowing users to choose which features show up on the bar would make the app far better.

Instagram has devolved from a platform for social connection into a surveillance machine that prioritizes profits over privacy. The app doesn't just collect the information you share-it digs into your location, browsing habits, and even offline activities.
This invasive data harvesting is not just unethical; it's an outright betrayal of user trust, turning us into products for advertisers rather than participants in a community.
What's even more disturbing is Meta’s integration into nearly every aspect of our digital lives. From logging into other services to its endless data sharing, the platform feels more like a monopoly than a social tool. It's a social app—not a government utility-yet it acts like it has authority over how we live online. Adding to this is Meta’s concerning relationship with the U.S. government, including lobbying efforts and questionable dealings like insider trading. These alliances raise serious ethical questions about how much influence Meta wields over public policy and opinion.
Even worse, Meta manipulates its users with algorithms designed to push divisive, inflammatory content to keep us scrolling, all while pretending to care about our well-being. The result is a platform that's not just invasive but toxic. Instagram is no longer about connection; it's about exploitation. It's time to seriously consider whether keeping this app is worth the cost of our privacy and autonomy.
